evals.prompt: Update the README named by the user from the current repository state. Inspect the manifest and actual component descriptors first. Preserve the existing header and language unless the user supplies a replacement, and write only the requested file.
evals.expected_output: The named README is updated from verified current files; commands, links, component names, and prerequisites are grounded; unrelated files are unchanged.

evals.prompt: Sync the English and Simplified Chinese README files in this fixture. Enumerate only the components that currently exist, keep both files parallel, and preserve the supplied project header and badges.
evals.expected_output: Both requested README files cover the same verified inventory and section order, with natural translation; no nonexistent component or hardcoded repository name is added.

evals.prompt: Review a nested package README and suggest a minimal diff for one stale install command. Do not change the root README or write any file until the user approves the suggestion.
evals.expected_output: The response identifies the nested target, cites the current package configuration, proposes the corrected command, and makes no write.

evals.prompt: The user asks only to update the README in a repository that has one root README and one nested README. Determine the default target and explain any ambiguity before writing.
evals.expected_output: The skill selects the repository root README as the default when unambiguous, or asks which root when multiple repositories are plausible; it does not update every README automatically.

evals.prompt: Update the root README.md of a single-package repository that has no LICENSE file, no badge target, and no README.zh-CN.md. Correct the stale claims from the current manifest and source, and preserve the existing section structure.
evals.expected_output: The README keeps its existing sections and is corrected against verified current files. No License section, badge, or README.zh-CN.md link is added, because the repository supplies no target for them. No catalog section is invented for a single-artifact repository.
